key_insight: Generative AI can produce multiple plausible turbulent flows from incomplete information, but physical fidelity requires validation beyond visual realism and low-order statistics.
engineering_relevance: Potential uses include stochastic closures, flow super-resolution, data assimilation, and uncertainty quantification for under-resolved turbulence.
method: Reviews diffusion, score-based, and related probability-transport models.
Examines flow generation, probabilistic reconstruction, reduced-order modeling, and temporal evolution.
Proposes physics-aware validation and a reproducible benchmark ecosystem.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports no quantitative model results; it advocates evaluation of energy transfer, intermittency, conservation, temporal consistency, ensemble diversity, and generalization.
watch_item: Limited data, inadequate baselines, and incomplete validation can conceal physically incorrect predictions.
paper_title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
